fun_highlights: The vocation × era intersection cards (vx_soldier_war, vx_maker_plenty, vx_scholar_turning) are the game's best content: a soldier born into a war year meets fundamentally different beats than one born in peacetime, and this is the clearest structural divergence the game delivers.

Callback chains — when they land — produce genuine 'one more run' pull. cb_books_late (reading the childhood book decades on), cb_lookaway (the stranger sleeping rough, the old cowardice resurfacing), cb_unspoken (writing the letter at last) feel earned and personal in a way static cards cannot.

The dynasty meta layer (seat 0–7, reputation types, heirlooms, motto crystallization) is a real cross-session goal. Watching 'Nothing was given; all was built' emerge for House Okonkwo or 'We burn bright, and we burn' for the Vasquez reckless line does create a sense of accumulation across lives.

Solitary and childless life-shapes are genuinely realized — Niall in Dynasty 7 choosing no children then reconsidering, Ingrid in Dynasty 10 choosing childless with clear eyes, Mira in Dynasty 8 ending alone — these feel like distinct structures, not foreclosures.

The trait-affinity system (a bookish child skewed toward c_book; a warm child toward c_friend) makes early childhood genuinely read differently per character, which is the most invisible feature and one of the best.

The era system changes the opening texture of each dynasty in ways that compound: a plague-era heir tending the sick (Aldous D12) lives a structurally different youth than a plenty-era heir riding the boom.
staleness: 'Red and furious and entirely unimpressed by any of it' appears for first-born children across at least 9 of the 15 dynasties in the transcript. The S._usedFurious guard fires once per dynasty but the dynasty scope is too narrow — across a long session this line lands in almost every dynasty and reads as the game's signature birth line, not a surprise.

The love → marriage → child → work promotion → midlife health → elder legacy arc is the skeleton of roughly 80% of lives by dynasties 8–15. The card texts rotate well but the structural beats arrive in the same order at the same life-stages in dynasty after dynasty. The replay-addict sees the chassis by dynasty 4 and spends the rest watching the upholstery change.

The 'outcast returns as somebody' callback (cb_outcast_return) fires in nearly every life that chose to befriend the lonely child. Because c_friend itself fires in almost every childhood, this means the callback fires in almost every life — it stops feeling like a meaningful reach-back and becomes an expected beat.

The adult band (ages 28–60) is still the thinnest in variety per-run. The repeatable filler cards (a_smallchoice, a_recognition, m_smaller_body, a_fallow, a_friend_drift) are well-written but they carry no memory of who the character is — they could happen to anyone. A soldier in midlife and a scholar in midlife get the same generic 'promotion or presence' and 'recognition' cards alongside their vocation cards.

The discovery layer is invisible. With ~150+ distinct cards, a replay-addict's central question is 'what haven't I seen yet?' — but the game surfaces no answer. There is no discovery log, no hint that rare cards exist, no way to know whether a solitary wanderer in a war era will unlock content you've never encountered. The pull to replay is present but diffuse rather than directed.

Mottos repeat across dynasties: 'What the mind holds cannot be taken' crystallizes in Dynasties 1, 3, 7, and 15 in this fifteen-dynasty run. 'We burn bright, and we burn' appears in Dynasties 4, 9, and 12. The freshPick variant selection prevents exact line repetition within a dynasty but does not prevent the same motto from becoming the dominant scholar/reckless house outcome across many runs.

The 'work promotion vs. presence' card (a_work) fires in many lives in mid-adulthood and its two lines — 'Worked for the family until the family barely saw them' vs. 'Said no to the title, and yes to the evenings' — become recognizable templates. By dynasty 10 the player knows which stat this card is optimizing for without reading the choice text.

improvements.what: Extend the S._usedFurious guard to a session-level set (e.g., RECENT_LINES already exists — add the birth line pool to it) so the 'red and furious' birth line cannot repeat within the same session regardless of dynasty boundaries.
improvements.why: This is the single most-repeated line in the transcript — 9 appearances in 15 dynasties. It is the first thing a player sees for most heirs and training it to be surprising is cheap (the pool exists; just widen the exclusion window).

improvements.what: Surface a 'moments witnessed' counter or constellation discovery map in the UI — even a simple 'X of Y moments seen this session' badge, or greyed-out star shapes in the constellation for card categories not yet encountered.
improvements.why: The game has ~150 cards but the player has no way to know this. A replay-addict's core motivation is exhausting a possibility space; without a visible frontier, the pull to keep playing is vague. Even a rough count ('you have seen 43 distinct moments') would transform passive replay into directed exploration.

improvements.what: Gate cb_outcast_return on a minimum bond threshold AND a minimum life-years gap (e.g., the friend must be at least 20 years older than when befriended), and lower its base weight from 4 to 2 so it fires less reliably. Add 1–2 alternative friendship callbacks with different flavors (a betrayal that resurfaces; a friend who simply stays ordinary).
improvements.why: The current callback fires so reliably it becomes an expected beat rather than a payoff. Lowering its fire rate and adding variety to what 'an early friendship echoes into' would make the callback feel earned rather than clockwork.

improvements.what: Add 3–4 adult-band cards that are gated on the intersection of vocation AND a personal memory (not just vocation OR a memory), so a scholar who also had the childhood book gets a different midlife beat than a scholar who didn't.
improvements.why: The adult band is the thinnest for character-specific divergence. A soldier-with-reckless-past and a soldier-without should diverge more in midlife than the current system allows. These intersections are the game's best content (cb_ chains, vx_ cards) and the adult band has fewer of them than childhood or elder.

improvements.what: Add 2–3 additional motto variants per reputation type so that a scholarly house has at least 5 possible mottos, and add a session-level exclusion so the same motto string cannot crystallize in two dynasties within the same session.
improvements.why: Motto crystallization is a high-moment event; seeing 'What the mind holds cannot be taken' four times in fifteen dynasties devalues it. The RECENT_LINES system already tracks recent epitaphs — applying the same logic to mottos is a small addition with meaningful payoff.

improvements.what: Add one or two 'deep cut' card chains that require 3+ specific memories across 2+ generations to unlock — content that a player who has seen everything else might stumble on in dynasty 12 having never seen it before.
improvements.why: The replay-addict's long-arc motivation is exhausting the possibility space. Cards that require unlikely multi-generation conditions (e.g., a scholar whose parent strayed AND who inherited the secret AND who also took a stand in youth) create genuine 'I've never seen this before' moments deep into a session, which is exactly what this profile needs.

verdict: A Life is pleasant and literary, and its card pool is larger and more varied than a first impression suggests, but by dynasty 5–6 a replay-addict has learned the chassis — love, calling, child, promotion, midlife health, elder legacy — and subsequent runs feel like the same template with rotating prose rather than structurally different lives; the invisible discovery layer and a handful of over-firing beats keep it below the 8 bar.
